prompt.context: Your client is Hotel Co., an international hotel corporation that owns and operates 2,700 hotels worldwide, as well as a separate timeshare business with 75 properties worldwide. Their hotel rooms are typically sold on a per night basis, whereas their timeshare properties are sold more like traditional homes via a mortgage which in turn gives the buyer the right to stay at a timeshare property for a set period of time each year. The CEO of Hotel Co. has approached you and has asked for guidance on whether or not they should spinoff their timeshare business into a separate standalone entity called Timeshare Co. Hotel Co. wants to weigh a few criteria, including the financial impact, risk, and strategic outlook. Hotel Co. only uses a five year timeframe for all financial decisions. Hotel Co. would be spun off and taken public, with 20% of the IPO proceeds being paid back to Hotel Co. The remainder of IPO proceeds would go to Timeshare Co. and the underwriters. Hotel Co.'s bankers think they can sell 10 million shares at $220 each.
prompt.question: Should Hotel Co. spin off its timeshare business into a separate standalone entity called Timeshare Co.? Evaluate the financial impact, risk, and strategic outlook.

clarifying_info.a: Hotel Co. wants to weigh financial impact, risk, and strategic outlook.

clarifying_info.q: What time horizon should we use?
clarifying_info.a: Hotel Co. only uses a five-year timeframe for all financial decisions.

clarifying_info.q: What are the IPO terms if Timeshare Co. is spun off?
clarifying_info.a: Hotel Co. would receive 20% of IPO proceeds. Bankers expect to sell 10 million shares at $220 each.

exhibits.title: Timeshare Co. Historic and Projected Profits
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing Timeshare Co. annual profit (in $M, bar chart) and US Home Sales % change (line chart) from 2007 through 2015, with years 2011-2015 marked as projections (asterisked).

exhibits.title: Mortgage Default Expectations
exhibits.shows: A table of Timeshare Co. mortgage default rates by year from 2007 to 2015, with years 2011-2015 marked as projections.

exhibits.title: Mortgage Portfolio's Contribution to Profits
exhibits.shows: A table showing the portion of Timeshare Co. total profits derived from its mortgage portfolio, by year from 2007 to 2015, with years 2011-2015 marked as projections.

framework: Financial impact: Compare 5-year projected profits of Timeshare Co. if kept in-house vs. IPO proceeds Hotel Co. would receive if spun off
Risk analysis: Assess volatility of Timeshare Co. revenue stream, driven by mortgage default rates and dependency of profits on mortgage portfolio
Strategic outlook: Evaluate cross-selling synergies between hotel and timeshare businesses, and whether alternative risk-mitigation options exist
Recommendation: Weigh financial closeness of the two options against risk reduction benefit of spinoff, and identify next steps

questions.prompt: Question 1 (Financial Impact): What is the financial decision-making process for whether or not to spin off Timeshare Co.? Use Exhibit 1.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that US home sales are a good proxy for Timeshare Co. revenues, and use the projected profit figures from Exhibit 1 to sum up 5-year profits. Candidate should then calculate 20% of IPO proceeds and compare the two figures. Strong answer notes the two amounts are very close, making the financial case alone inconclusive.

math.setup: Sum 5-year projected profits (2011-2015) from Exhibit 1. Then calculate Hotel Co.'s 20% share of IPO proceeds (10M shares x $220/share).
steps: Comparison: $450M (keep) vs. $440M (spin off) — difference of only $10M
math.answer: Keeping Timeshare Co. in-house yields $450M over 5 years vs. $440M from the IPO. The financial difference is negligible, so financial impact alone does not strongly favor either decision.

questions.prompt: Question 2 (Risk): What is the risk decision-making process for whether or not to spin off Timeshare Co.? Use Exhibits 2 and 3.
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe from Exhibit 2 that default rates spiked sharply in 2008/2009 and have not returned to pre-2008 levels (a 'new floor' appears to have been established around 4.3-4.5%). From Exhibit 3, candidate should note that mortgages consistently represent ~94-97% of Timeshare Co. revenues, making the business heavily exposed to default rate risk. Strong answer concludes that the revenue projections in Exhibit 1 are highly uncertain and that spinning off removes this risk from Hotel Co.'s balance sheet. Bonus: candidate proposes alternative risk mitigants such as referring buyers to external mortgage companies for a finder's fee, or purchasing mortgage default insurance.

questions.prompt: Question 3 (Strategic Outlook / Recommendation): What is your recommendation and what are the next steps?
questions.guidance: Strong candidate synthesizes: (1) IPO proceeds are only slightly less than 5-year expected profits but profits are extremely volatile; (2) spinning off also achieves risk reduction; therefore spinning off is the preferred choice. Next steps should include examining cross-selling impact (how many timeshares are sold to hotel customers, and how cross-selling can continue post-spinoff) and evaluating other risk-reduction alternatives before finalizing the decision.

brainstorming.prompt: What are alternative ways Hotel Co. could reduce the risk of its mortgage portfolio without fully spinning off Timeshare Co.?

categories.name: Shift mortgage exposure
ideas: Connect timeshare buyers with external mortgage companies and collect a finder's fee rather than carrying mortgages in-house
Partner with a bank or financial institution to originate and hold the mortgages

categories.name: Insurance and hedging
ideas: Buy mortgage default insurance to reduce portfolio volatility
Use financial derivatives or credit default swaps to hedge default risk

categories.name: Portfolio management
ideas: Tighten underwriting standards to reduce default probability
Diversify timeshare locations to reduce geographic concentration risk

categories.name: Business model changes
ideas: Shift timeshare sales to a rental/points model to reduce mortgage dependency
Reduce LTV ratios on new timeshare mortgages to improve collateral coverage

recommendation: Recommend spinning off Timeshare Co.: IPO proceeds to Hotel Co. ($440M) are only slightly below the 5-year expected profits ($450M), while the profit projections carry substantial risk and volatility
Spinning off also achieves a meaningful reduction in Hotel Co.'s exposure to mortgage default rate risk, which appears to have settled at a structurally higher 'new normal' of ~4.3-4.5%
risks: 5-year profit projections may be overly optimistic; actual upside could significantly exceed $450M if the housing market recovers faster than expected, making the spinoff more costly in hindsight
Spinning off may sever cross-selling synergies between Hotel Co. and Timeshare Co., reducing overall customer value and revenue for both entities
Underwriters and market conditions may not support the $220/share IPO price, reducing proceeds below $440M
next_steps: Quantify cross-selling revenue between hotel customers and timeshare purchases; model how much can be preserved via commercial agreements post-spinoff
Evaluate alternative risk-mitigation options (finder's fee model, default insurance) to determine if risk can be adequately managed without a full spinoff
Conduct due diligence on IPO market conditions and validate banker assumptions on share price and demand
